taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.
taskVersion.definition:
@kbench.task(
    name="deadline-math-hard-reasoned",
    # Literal y de 255 caracteres como mÃ¡ximo: Kaggle rechaza la task si no.
    description=(
        "Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when "
        "the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth "
        "computed with zoneinfo."
    ),
)
def deadline_math(llm) -> float:
    passed = 0
    for case in CASE_SETS[SET]:
        response, output_tokens = ask(llm, case)
        answer = parse_answer(response)
        # Sin lÃ­nea final y al borde del lÃ­mite: se cortÃ³. Cuenta como fallo, pero se marca para el anÃ¡lisis.
        truncated = answer is None and output_tokens >= 0.95 * MAX_TOKENS
        kbench.assertions.assert_equal(
            case.expected, answer,
            expectation=f"[{case.category}] {case.id}: {case.statement} -> {case.reader} = {case.expected}"
            + (f" (truncated at max_tokens={MAX_TOKENS})" if truncated else ""),
        )
        passed += answer == case.expected
    # ProporciÃ³n de aciertos: Kaggle aÃºn no muestra Â«aciertos de totalÂ» (lee la tupla como valor Â± intervalo).
    return passed / len(CASE_SETS[SET])

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the deadline in Madrid local time.

The deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time).

In late October, I need to check daylight saving time:
- **Pacific Time**: In the US, DST ends on the first Sunday of November 2026 (November 1, 2026). So on October 30, 2026, the US is still on PDT (UTC-7).
- **Madrid (CET/CEST)**: In Europe, DST ends on the last Sunday of October 2026, which is October 25, 2026. So by October 30, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

So the offset from PT to Madrid time:
- PT is UTC-7 (PDT)
- Madrid is UTC+1 (CET)
- Difference: 8 hours ahead

11:59 PM PDT on October 30 = 23:59 + 8 hours = 07:59 on October 31, 2026, Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when "this coming Monday" after Friday, October 30, 2026 is, and convert 10:00 AM Los Angeles time to Madrid time.

**Step 1: Find the date of "this coming Monday"**
Friday, October 30, 2026 → the coming Monday is November 2, 2026.

**Step 2: Determine time zones on November 2, 2026**

- **Los Angeles (Pacific Time):** In 2026, US daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026 (first Sunday in November). So on Monday, November 2, Los Angeles is on PST (UTC-8).

- **Madrid (Central European Time):** In 2026, European daylight saving time ends on Sunday, October 25, 2026 (last Sunday in October). So by November 2, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

**Step 3: Convert**
10:00 AM PST = 10:00 + 8 hours = 18:00 UTC
18:00 UTC + 1 hour = 19:00 CET (Madrid time)

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to determine when the hackathon ends, starting from Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time, lasting exactly 48 hours.

First, let me consider the time zone situation. Madrid uses CET/CEST. In 2026, the clocks fall back from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026, at 3:00 AM local time.

So the hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 CEST (UTC+2).

Let me convert to UTC and work from there:
- Start: October 24, 18:00 CEST = October 24, 16:00 UTC
- Add 48 hours: October 26, 16:00 UTC

Now convert back to Madrid local time on October 26:
- Since the clocks fell back on October 25 at 3:00 AM, Madrid is now on CET (UTC+1) on October 26.
- October 26, 16:00 UTC = October 26, 17:00 CET

So the hackathon ends at 17:00 local Madrid time on Monday, October 26, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert the deadline from PT to Madrid local time.

**Step 1: Find the deadline in PT.**
The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT. Adding 72 hours (3 days) gives:
October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT.

**Step 2: Determine which PT offset applies.**
October 29, 2026 is before the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026), so the US is still on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT = UTC−7).

So the deadline is October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PDT = 17:00 UTC.

**Step 3: Determine Madrid's offset.**
Madrid follows CET/CEST. Clocks fall back the last Sunday of October, which in 2026 is October 25. So by October 29, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

**Step 4: Convert.**
17:00 UTC = 18:00 CET.

The deadline in Madrid is October 29, 2026 at 18:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when results are announced in Madrid local time.

**Step 1: Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET.**

ET here means Eastern Time. On October 31, 2026, we need to check if it's EDT or EST. Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on the first Sunday of November 2026, which is November 1, 2026. So on October 31, 2026, the US is still on EDT (UTC-4).

So submissions close: October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT = November 1, 2026 at 03:59 UTC.

**Step 2: Add 36 hours to get the announcement time.**

November 1, 2026 at 03:59 UTC + 36 hours = November 2, 2026 at 15:59 UTC.

**Step 3: Convert to Madrid local time.**

Now I need to check Madrid's time zone on November 2, 2026. Europe changes clocks on the last Sunday of October. The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026. So by November 2, Madrid is on CET (Central European Time) = UTC+1.

November 2, 2026 at 15:59 UTC = November 2, 2026 at 16:59 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert Unix timestamp 1791788340 to Tokyo local time (JST = UTC+9).

Let me work through this:

Unix timestamp 1791788340 seconds from epoch (January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC).

Let me estimate the year. 
- Seconds per year ≈ 31,536,000 (non-leap) or 31,622,400 (leap)
- 1791788340 / 31,536,000 ≈ 56.82 years after 1970 → roughly 2026

Let me be more precise. Seconds through end of 2025:
- From 1970 to 2025 is 55 years
- Leap years between 1970-2024: 1972,1976,1980,1984,1988,1992,1996,2000,2004,2008,2012,2016,2020,2024 = 14 leap years
- Days = 55×365 + 14 = 20075 + 14 = 20089 days
- Seconds through end of 2025 = 20089 × 86400 = 1,735,689,600

Remaining: 1,791,788,340 - 1,735,689,600 = 56,098,740 seconds into 2026.

Days into 2026: 56,098,740 / 86400 = 649.29... days

Wait, that's more than 365 days, so it goes into 2027.

2026 is not a leap year (365 days = 31,536,000 seconds).
56,098,740 - 31,536,000 = 24,562,740 seconds into 2027.

Days into 2027: 24,562,740 / 86400 = 284.29... days

284 full days = 284 days from Jan 1.

Month breakdown for 2027 (not a leap year):
- Jan: 31 (total: 31)
- Feb: 28 (total: 59)
- Mar: 31 (total: 90)
- Apr: 30 (total: 120)
- May: 31 (total: 151)
- Jun: 30 (total: 181)
- Jul: 31 (total: 212)
- Aug: 31 (total: 243)
- Sep: 30 (total: 273)
- Oct: 31 (total: 304)

284 days: that falls in October. 284 - 273 = 11, so October 11.

Remaining seconds: 24,562,740 - 284×86400 = 24,562,740 - 24,537,600 = 25,140 seconds.

25,140 / 3600 = 6 hours, remainder 25,140 - 21,600 = 3,540 seconds
3,540 / 60 = 59 minutes, remainder 0 seconds.

So in UTC: 2027-10-11 06:59:00

Convert to JST (UTC+9): 2027-10-11 15:59:00

ANSWER: 2027-10-11 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from UTC (Z) to Madrid local time.

Madrid is in the CET/CEST time zone. I need to determine whether daylight saving time (CEST, UTC+2) or standard time (CET, UTC+1) applies on October 25, 2026.

In the EU, clocks fall back on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, October 25 is a Sunday. The clocks go back from 3:00 AM CEST to 2:00 AM CET on that day.

The deadline is 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z (2:30 AM UTC).

At 2:30 AM UTC on October 25, 2026, has the clock change already happened? The change happens at 3:00 AM CEST, which is 1:00 AM UTC. So by 2:30 AM UTC, the clocks have already fallen back to standard time (CET, UTC+1).

So Madrid is at UTC+1 at that point:
2:30 AM UTC + 1 hour = 3:30 AM CET on October 25, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the last Sunday of October 2026 and convert 11:59 PM Pacific Time to Madrid local time.

**Last Sunday of October 2026:**
October 2026 starts on a Thursday. Let me find the Sundays:
- Oct 4, 11, 18, 25 are Sundays.
So the last Sunday of October 2026 is **October 25, 2026**.

**Time zone conversion:**

Now I need to consider daylight saving time rules:

- **Pacific Time:** DST ends on the first Sunday of November 2026 (Nov 1). So on Oct 25, Pacific Time is still PDT (UTC-7).
- **Madrid (CET/CEST):** Europe changes clocks on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that's October 25. Clocks fall back at 3:00 AM local time (going to 2:00 AM). So the change happens in the early morning of Oct 25.

So on the night of October 25 at 11:59 PM:
- Pacific Time is PDT = UTC-7
- Madrid has already fallen back to CET = UTC+1

11:59 PM PDT = 23:59 UTC-7 = 06:59 UTC (next day, Oct 26)
In Madrid (UTC+1): 06:59 + 1 = 07:59 on October 26.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to figure out when the US ends daylight saving time in 2026, and then convert the deadline to Lima, Peru local time.

**Step 1: When does the US end daylight saving time in 2026?**

The US ends daylight saving time (falls back) on the first Sunday in November. In 2026, November 1 is a Sunday. So DST ends on **November 1, 2026**.

**Step 2: What is Eastern Time at that moment?**

The deadline is "12:00 noon Eastern Time" on that day. Since the clocks fall back at 2:00 AM on November 1, by noon the US will be on Eastern Standard Time (EST), which is UTC-5.

**Step 3: What is Lima's time zone?**

Lima, Peru is on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 year-round (Peru does not observe daylight saving time).

**Step 4: Convert**

Since both EST and Lima time are UTC-5, the deadline is 12:00 noon in Lima as well.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) corresponds to UTC-12, the last time zone on Earth. So "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" means the end of December 31, 2026, in UTC-12, which is equivalent to:

- January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC-12
- January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC (adding 12 hours)

Tokyo is UTC+9 (JST), so I add 9 hours to UTC:

- January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC + 9 hours = January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026 to New York time.

**Sydney time on October 5, 2026:**
October 5 is during Australia's daylight saving time (AEDT = UTC+11). Sydney DST starts the first Sunday of October in 2026, which is October 4, 2026. So on October 5, Sydney is on AEDT (UTC+11).

Wait, let me double-check: Australia's DST starts the first Sunday of October. October 1, 2026 is a Thursday, so the first Sunday is October 4, 2026. DST typically starts at 2:00 AM on that Sunday, so by October 5, Sydney is on AEDT (UTC+11).

**New York time on October 5, 2026:**
US DST ends the first Sunday of November, so on October 5, New York is still on EDT (UTC-4).

**Conversion:**
- 5:00 PM AEDT = 17:00 UTC+11 = 06:00 UTC on October 5, 2026
- 06:00 UTC = 02:00 EDT (UTC-4) on October 5, 2026

So the deadline is 2:00 AM on October 5, 2026, New York time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
